records.label: Affected sibs with Bruck syndrome

phenotypes.text: underhydroxylation of telopeptide lysine residues of bone collagen type I
normal crosslinking in cartilage and ligament

records.segregation: All affected sibs shared a cluster of haplotypes identical by descent on chromosome 17p12
quotes: We report that lysine residues within the telopeptides of collagen type I in bone are underhydroxylated, leading to aberrant crosslinking, but that the lysine residues in the triple helix are normally modified.
In contrast to bone, cartilage and ligament show unaltered telopeptide hydroxylation as evidenced by normal patterns of crosslinking.

records.label: Bruck syndrome patients with PLOD2 exon 17 missense mutations

variants.as_reported: two missense mutations in exon 17 of PLOD2

quotes: By analyzing the genetic defect of Bruck syndrome, which is characterized by a pyridinoline deficiency in bone collagen, we found two missense mutations in exon 17 of PLOD2, thereby identifying PLOD2 as a putative TLH gene.

records.label: Boy with Bruck syndrome

phenotypes.text: low urinary collagen crosslink degradation products

quotes: We report on a boy who had congenital contractures with pterygia at birth and severe OI-like osteopenia and multiple fractures.

His urine contained high amounts of hydroxyproline but low amounts of collagen crosslinks degradation products; and he was shown to be homozygous for a novel mutation leading to an Arg598His substitution in PLOD2.

records.label: Two Bruck syndrome probands with homozygous PLOD2 exon 13a frameshift

phenotypes.text: Bruck syndrome (osteogenesis imperfecta-like bone fragility with congenital joint contractures)

variants.as_reported: homozygous frameshift mutation in the alternative exon 13a of PLOD2

quotes: Herein, we sought mutations in six consanguineous BS families and detected changes in either PLOD2 or FKBP10 in all cases.

Two probands were found with a homozygous frameshift mutation in the alternative exon 13a of PLOD2, indicating that specific inactivation of the longer protein isoform encoded by this gene is sufficient to cause BS.

records.label: Patient with AR-OI and homozygous PLOD2 donor splice site mutation

variants.as_reported: homozygous donor splice site mutation in PLOD2

quotes: by homozygosity mapping, followed by a candidate gene approach, we identified a homozygous donor splice site mutation in PLOD2 in a patient with autosomal-recessive OI (AR-OI).

records.label: Two brothers with compound heterozygous PLOD2 mutations
quotes: Screening of additional samples also revealed compound heterozygous mutations in PLOD2 in two brothers, one affected with mild AR-OI and the other with mild BS.

notes.statement: Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) concluded that PLOD2 mutations cause not only Bruck syndrome but also autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta phenotypes of variable severity, with intrafamilial variability between BS and mild AR-OI in brothers with the same compound heterozygous genotype.
quotes: Thus, PLOD2 in addition to causing BS is also associated with AR-OI phenotypes of variable severity.
compound heterozygous mutations in PLOD2 in two brothers, one affected with mild AR-OI and the other with mild BS.

notes.statement: Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) found homozygous frameshift mutations in the alternative exon 13a of PLOD2 in 2 Bruck syndrome probands, indicating that specific inactivation of the longer PLOD2 protein isoform is sufficient to cause Bruck syndrome.
quotes: Two probands were found with a homozygous frameshift mutation in the alternative exon 13a of PLOD2, indicating that specific inactivation of the longer protein isoform encoded by this gene is sufficient to cause BS.

notes.statement: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) noted that the Arg598His mutation in PLOD2 was adjacent to the 2 previously reported mutations (Gly601Val and Thr608Ile), suggesting a functionally important hotspot in PLOD2.
quotes: The mutation is adjacent to the two mutations previously reported (Gly601Val and Thr608Ile), suggesting a functionally important hotspot in PLOD2.

notes.statement: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) suggested that the combination of pterygia with bone fragility indicates that telopeptide lysyl hydroxylation must be involved in prenatal joint formation and morphogenesis.
quotes: The combination of pterygia with bone fragility, as illustrated by this case, is difficult to explain; it suggests that telopeptide lysyl hydroxylation must be involved in prenatal joint formation and morphogenesis.

notes.statement: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) proposed that urinary collagen degradation products and PLOD2 mutation analysis may be used to diagnose Bruck syndrome and distinguish it from osteogenesis imperfecta.
quotes: Collagen degradation products in urine and mutation analysis of PLOD2 may be used to diagnose BS and differentiate it from OI.

notes.statement: In patients with Bruck syndrome, which has a pyridinoline deficiency in bone collagen, van der Slot et al. (2003) found 2 missense mutations in exon 17 of the PLOD2 gene. They proposed that PLOD2 is a putative telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase (TLH) gene.
quotes: By analyzing the genetic defect of Bruck syndrome, which is characterized by a pyridinoline deficiency in bone collagen, we found two missense mutations in exon 17 of PLOD2, thereby identifying PLOD2 as a putative TLH gene.

notes.statement: van der Slot et al. (2003) found highly increased PLOD2 mRNA levels in fibroblasts from the fibrotic skin of patients with systemic sclerosis. The matrix deposited by these fibroblasts also had more pyridinoline cross-links, which linked PLOD2 mRNA levels to the hydroxylation of lysine residues in collagen telopeptides.
quotes: we investigated fibroblasts derived from fibrotic skin of systemic sclerosis (SSc) patients and found that PLOD2 mRNA is highly increased indeed

increased pyridinoline cross-link levels were found in the matrix deposited by SSc fibroblasts, demonstrating a clear link between mRNA levels of the putative TLH gene (PLOD2) and the hydroxylation of lysine residues within the telopeptides

notes.statement: Bank et al. (1999) described Bruck syndrome as characterized by osteoporosis, joint contractures, fragile bones, and short stature.
quotes: Bruck syndrome is characterized by the presence of osteoporosis, joint contractures, fragile bones, and short stature.

notes.statement: Bank et al. (1999) found that in Bruck syndrome, lysine residues within the telopeptides of bone collagen type I were underhydroxylated, leading to aberrant crosslinking, whereas helical lysines were normally modified; cartilage and ligament showed unaltered telopeptide hydroxylation and normal crosslinking patterns.
quotes: We report that lysine residues within the telopeptides of collagen type I in bone are underhydroxylated, leading to aberrant crosslinking, but that the lysine residues in the triple helix are normally modified.
In contrast to bone, cartilage and ligament show unaltered telopeptide hydroxylation as evidenced by normal patterns of crosslinking.

notes.statement: Bank et al. (1999) concluded that collagen crosslinking is regulated primarily by tissue-specific enzymes that hydroxylate only telopeptide lysine residues, and proposed that Bruck syndrome results from deficiency of a bone-specific telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase.
quotes: The results provide compelling evidence that collagen crosslinking is regulated primarily by tissue-specific enzymes that hydroxylate only telopeptide lysine residues and not those destined for the helical portion of the molecule.

notes.statement: By a genome screen, Bank et al. (1999) identified only a single region, on chromosome 17p12, where all affected sibs shared a cluster of haplotypes identical by descent, suggesting this might be the Bruck syndrome locus and the location of the bone telopeptidyl lysyl hydroxylase.
quotes: A genome screen identified only a single region on chromosome 17p12 where all affected sibs shared a cluster of haplotypes identical by descent; this might be the BS (Bruck syndrome) locus and consequently the region where bone telopeptidyl lysyl hydroxylase is located.
